correctness.rationale: The normalized support set is compact after allowing adjacent collisions. On each collision stratum the Lagrange condition for the third moment is quadratic, so no interior extremum can have three distinct levels. All global extrema therefore reduce to contiguous two-level coarsenings. Their skewness is g(P), strictly increasing in the lower-block mass P, giving endpoint masses p1 and pm as the sharp limits. Connectedness fills the interior, and the sample covariance identity is exact.

broader_coverage.reasoning: These sources explain why parent skewness controls the sampling relationship, but treating the parent distribution as given does not determine the full skewness range when only its ordered atom probabilities are fixed.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete sharp classification of a basic standardized moment under a natural fixed categorical probability profile. It also yields a support-robust sign criterion for the classical sample-mean/sample-variance relationship, including the non-obvious fact that a majority endpoint mass forces the sign for every increasing numerical coding.
